review: program.py assigns positive ordinary hierarchy tags monotonically in one pre-discovery pass. Later invalid imported classes can be reset to zero; newly specialized generic ClassInfo objects begin untagged. The only tag assignments are the initial marking/numbering, ClassInfo zero initialization and bad_class zeroing.

calls.gen_new_obj stores the same ClassInfo.tag in every constructed tagged object. declarations.gen_getfield uses the table only for ordinary positive-tag hierarchies, and retains pys_exc_cls for exception classes.

Table construction indexes each positive ClassInfo.tag directly to sconst(short(ClassInfo.name)); the lookup uses the loaded runtime object tag without recoding. The base fallback is therefore covered by the same registry-to-object/table invariant as descendants, rather than inferred from mere presence of its name in the table.

The8 current-tree field tests check all positive registry tag/name pairs, independent families, excluded tag holes, zero-tag template specializations, first table creation during dry(), exact/no-read controls and deterministic emission. Optional qualification ran these with44 normal/program-GC JIT/AOT comparisons across11 class, field, slots and copyreg fixtures; recorded compiler/source identities match this audit.

The existing per-module correspondence helper separately confirms every explicit old selected-tag/name pair and unchanged residual module content after only witnessed checkout-string paths plus explicit string/local renumbering. Its fallback/domain limitation remains stated; runtime correctness is supported by the source invariant review and current-tree tests, not normalization alone.
